items.entity: Supports at the base of the design domain
items.description: 'Structures optimization': 'As shown on the right of Fig. 6, the points at the base of the design domain are fixed'. The text does not say which degrees of freedom are fixed (clamped vs vertical only) or whether all bottom-face nodes are fixed. The detail is only in Fig. 6 (right).
readings: All nodes on the bottom face (z=0) clamped in x, y and z
All bottom-face nodes fixed in z only (frictionless roller), plus minimal in-plane constraints to stop rigid-body motion
Only bottom-face nodes that belong to solid (rho~1) voxels are clamped

items.entity: Distributed compressive load on the top surface
items.description: 'Structures optimization': under 'compression loading', 'the top surface is subjected to distributed forces generated by placing a thin shell at the top of the design domain'. The text does not say how the distributed force is split over the nodes or at which nodes it acts. The detail is only in Fig. 6 (right).
readings: Uniform pressure over the whole top face, applied as consistent nodal loads (interior 1, edge 1/2, corner 1/4) on the outer face of the shell
Equal downward force at every one of the 41x41 top-face nodes
Load applied at the nodes where the shell meets the design region instead of the outer top face

items.description: No force or pressure value is given anywhere for the Fig. 6/7 setup. The absolute compliance values in Fig. 7c depend on it.
readings: Total resultant force = 1 spread over the top face
Unit force per top-face node
Unit pressure on the top face (resultant = face area)

items.entity: Thin load-spreading shell at the top of the design domain
items.description: 'Structures optimization': a 'thin shell' is placed at the top of the design domain to spread the load. The text does not give its thickness, whether it takes the place of the top voxel layer(s) of the 40x40x40 grid or sits on top as an extra layer, or whether it is solid material outside the design. It is only shown in Fig. 6 (right).
readings: Top 1 voxel layer of the 40^3 grid (z in [39/40,1]) fixed as solid (rho=1), not designable
One extra solid voxel layer added above the 40^3 design grid (40x40x41 FE mesh)
Passive solid layer two voxels thick at the top
No physical layer; load applied directly to the top design voxels

items.entity: Stiffness of the thin top shell
items.description: The material of the load-spreading shell is not given. The text only states E=1.0 for solid elements, nu=0.3 for all elements and Emin=1e-3 ('Structures optimization').
readings: Same as the solid: E=1.0, nu=0.3
Much stiffer, nearly rigid plate (e.g., E=1000)
Rigid tie: all top nodes forced to share one vertical displacement

items.entity: Whether the shell counts in the volume fraction
items.description: The target volume fractions (0.3, 0.35, 0.4, 0.45, 0.5) are given. The text does not say whether the passive shell volume is included in V=sum(rho_e v_e) and in the reference domain volume. A one-voxel layer is 2.5% of the domain, a large share of a 0.3 material budget.
readings: Volume fraction measured over all elements, including the shell
Volume fraction measured over the design (non-shell) voxels only

items.description: The text and Eq. (22) state V <= V0. The method actually minimizes c/c0 + mu(V/V0-1)^2 (Eq. 23, mu starting at 10 and rising by 1 per iteration to 500). That two-sided penalty acts like an equality and allows small violations.
readings: Hard inequality V <= V0 (OC/MMA)
Hard equality V = V0
Quadratic penalty of Eq. (23) with the stated mu ramp

items.entity: Physical size of the 40x40x40 voxel design domain
items.description: The FE grid is 40x40x40 voxels ('Structures optimization') and the network is defined on the unit cube [0,1]^3 (Methods). The element edge length used in the FEA is never stated, so absolute compliance values (Fig. 7c) cannot be matched.
readings: Unit cube, element edge 1/40
Cube of 40 units, element edge 1

items.entity: Exponent p in the Young's modulus interpolation (SIMP penalty)
items.description: 'Structures optimization' says the modulus comes from 'p-norm weighted interpolation' between Emax=1.0 and Emin=1e-3 but gives no p. Methods Eq. (12) only says p 'is set as 3 in most cases'.
readings: p = 1 (linear; the projection already pushes densities to 0/1)

items.description: 'Structures optimization' says 'the SDF values are filtered and projected'. The text does not say whether the density filter of Eqs. (13)-(14) is used in this example, and never gives its radius r_d. Only the projections (Eqs. 15-16) are specified.
readings: No spatial filter (projections only)
Cone density filter, r_d = 1.5 voxel widths
Cone density filter, r_d = 2 voxel widths
Cone density filter, r_d = 3 voxel widths

items.entity: First projection from network SDF to rho_bar (Eq. 15)
items.description: Eq. (15) prints a product, rho_bar = (e^(-alpha s)-1)(e^(alpha s)+1), which equals -2 sinh(alpha s). The problem statement after Eq. (17) prints rho_bar = e^(alpha s)-1, which reverses the sign so solid maps to low density. With alpha=2, both can push rho from Eq. (16) outside [0,1]. A ratio form is probably intended.
readings: rho_bar = (e^(-alpha s)-1)/(e^(-alpha s)+1) = -tanh(alpha s/2) (probably intended ratio)
rho_bar = (e^(-alpha s)-1)(e^(alpha s)+1), as printed in Eq. (15)
rho_bar = e^(alpha s)-1, as printed in the problem statement

items.entity: Schedule for the projection sharpness beta
items.description: Methods: 'start from beta=1.0 and increase its value by beta=4.0 after every 30 iterations until it reaches 128'. It is unclear whether 4 is added or multiplied; neither +4 nor x4 lands exactly on 128.
readings: beta <- beta + 4 every 30 iterations, capped at 128 (about 960 iterations)
beta <- 4*beta every 30 iterations (1, 4, 16, 64, then capped at 128)
beta <- 2*beta every 30 iterations (1, 2, 4, ..., 128)

items.entity: Optimizer settings (Adam on the latent code)
items.description: Methods: the latent code z is updated with Adam through backpropagation, but no learning rate or beta1/beta2 is given. A density-based re-run would also need its own update scheme and move limit.
readings: Adam, lr = 1e-3, default beta1/beta2
Adam, lr = 1e-2
Adam, lr = 5e-4 (same as network training)
Standard OC (move limit 0.2) or MMA, if a per-voxel density solver is used

items.description: No total iteration count or convergence tolerance is given; the histories appear only in Fig. 7d-e. The mu ramp alone takes 490 iterations, and the beta schedule takes about 120-960 iterations depending on how it is read.
readings: Stop 30 iterations after beta reaches 128
Fixed 500 iterations (until mu reaches 500)
Run until the relative change in L_TO is below 1e-4 after both ramps finish

items.entity: Design variables (latent space of a trained network)
items.description: 'Structures optimization' and Methods: the design variables are the 128-dimensional latent code of an MLP (5 layers of 512, ReLU, tanh output) trained on either the full dataset (1,960 structures) or the expert-filtered one (132 structures); Fig. 7 compares the two. The network weights, the random dataset generation and the expert filtering cannot be reproduced from the text. The isovalues are also described two ways: 'randomly sampled' vs fixed C_d/C_t lists. So the design space for a structured-grid solver is not defined.
readings: Free per-voxel SIMP densities on the 40^3 grid
Rebuild both datasets, retrain both networks with the stated hyperparameters, and optimize the 128-dimensional latent code
Optimize the TPMS blend weights w1-w7 and the isovalue C_d/C_t directly

items.entity: Starting structure for the Fig. 7 runs
items.description: 'Mechanical stiffness': the starting structure is 'randomly selected from the filtered dataset' and shown only as the left-most image in Fig. 7a&b. Its blend weights, solid/sheet type, isovalue and starting volume fraction are not given. The initial latent codes (and c0) depend on it.
readings: The specific structure from Fig. 7a (parameters unknown), voxelized on the 40^3 grid
Uniform density equal to the target volume fraction (standard SIMP start)
Some other filtered-type TPMS blend used as a stand-in starting design

items.description: The structures are TPMS-type unit cells (one period in the unit cube) that are later repeated periodically for printing (Fig. 9, Discussion). No periodic design constraint or periodic boundary condition is mentioned for the 40^3 optimization, and a free density solver would not produce periodicity on its own.
readings: No periodicity constraint; lateral faces traction-free
Periodic design constraint (densities match on opposite faces) so cells tile
Periodic displacement boundary conditions on the four lateral faces
